blacklistabilityReview.evidence: The deployment-materiality rule in docs/blacklist-tracker.md states: 'A control on a deployment below that share of circulating supply is recorded in the review evidence but does not set the verdict'; semantic.materiality.deploymentMaterialSharePct is 10%. The Pharos supply observation at Unix 1792269954 on 2026-10-17 reports Ethereum 96.103869%, BSC 1.592130%, Fantom 0.411624% and Avalanche 0.055162%; the latter three total 2.058916%, not material deployments under that rule. Canonical Ethereum DOLA's verified immutable source has no blacklist, pause, forced transfer, privileged holder burn or upgrade hook; burn(uint256) burns only msg.sender. Its existence is independently pinned by the creation receipt at Ethereum block 11915875 (2021-02-23T21:39:17Z), and its fixed runtime was re-read at block 26214783 (2026-10-17T20:51:59Z). Peripheral controls remain disclosed, not erased: at BSC block 128237994 (2026-10-17T20:55:49Z), isMinter(0x58892974758a4013377a45fad698d2ff1f08d98e) was true and burn(address(1),0) impersonating that minter succeeded, but this address is an AnyswapV6Router contract, not an EOA. Its external burn routes use the caller's balance, so impersonating the router does not prove arbitrary-holder burn reach from its actual external callers. At BSC block 128241702 (2026-10-17T21:23:37Z), DELAY() was 172800 seconds and pendingMinter/delayMinter were zero: zero means no pending minter change, while new minters require two-day set/apply admission. At Fantom block 123720210 (2026-10-17T20:53:24Z), owner/listed minter 0xc564ee9f21ed8a2d8e7e76c085740d5e4c5fafbe had empty runtime and an authorized burn(address(1),0) succeeded; this proves a peripheral authorization surface, not key availability or destruction of a nonzero victim balance. Avalanche's verified AnyswapV6ERC20 source also retains privileged mint/burn and mutable admission (block 97826123, 2026-10-17T21:23:32Z), but its sub-threshold deployment does not set the asset verdict. Upstream reserve test (2026-10-19): docs/blacklist-tracker.md requires strictly more than 50% of reserve composition to be exposed to issuer- or custodian-controlled yes, upstream or possible assets. DOLA's dominant reserve rows are FiRM debt secured by Curve LP tokens, so each LP is split into its constituents rather than attributing the whole row to its non-DOLA leg. At Ethereum block 26224508 (hash 0x17aedf7e36f56fd1dded72fccc0586ec0019895aab30138b39d35f5d81c2449d, 2026-10-19T05:23:35Z), Curve balances() multiplied by stored_rates() put the external leg at 24.194874% sUSDe in DOLA/sUSDe pool 0x744793b5110f6ca9cc7cdfe1ce16677c3eb192ef, 22.836453% sUSDS in DOLA/sUSDS pool 0x8b83c4aa949254895507d09365229bc3a8c7f710, 24.435149% scrvUSD in scrvUSD/sDOLA pool 0x76a962ba6770068bcf454d34dde17175611e6637, 74.005917% reUSD in reUSD/sDOLA pool 0x48d670d189b4b48757992d36897bca6e3f889040 and 99.645434% USR in DOLA/USR pool 0x38de22a3175708d45e7c7c64cd78479c8b56f76e; the remainder is DOLA or sDOLA self-exposure and does not count. Attributing each FiRM market's on-chain totalDebt() pro rata to those constituents, counting sUSDe and USR at Yes and conservatively including sUSDS, scrvUSD, reUSD and DAI as qualifying collateral, and adding direct sUSDe, WBTC and cbBTC collateral gives 19,687,326.59 DOLA of debt-equivalent exposure: 26.395288% of 74,586,519.70 DOLA net face claims (113,058,118.24 minted less 38,471,598.54 idle in the 49 API-listed FiRM markets, the reserve sidecar's denominator) and 27.618240% of 71,283,785.32 DOLA FiRM debt. Weighting the same pool fractions by FiRM TVL API collateral values (2026-10-19T05:21:04Z) gives about 26.180472% of gross collateral. The 2026-10-19 re-review leaves sUSDS and scrvUSD at Possible and reUSD at No; the calculation conservatively includes all three and DAI, and excluding any of them only lowers the qualifying share. Counting sUSDS, whose Ethereum controls are Sky governance only, is conservative. The upstream threshold is therefore not met. The exposure is disclosed, not dismissed: Ethena's FULL_RESTRICTED_STAKER_ROLE can restrict the 11,683,544.28 sUSDe held by the DOLA/sUSDe pool, which would block swaps and proportional withdrawals while one-coin DOLA withdrawal remains available. An external-only denominator that removes the DOLA and sDOLA legs would instead give 71.357943% of external collateral value, or 78.675323% of external net-claim and 90.638234% of external FiRM-debt debt-equivalent; that is not the documented reserve-composition test.

oracleRisk.summary: G1-3/G1-4: standard-external ('a standard external feed') replaces redundant-with-failover ('redundant feeds with automatic failover'; stablecoin-detail-oracle-client.ts). At Ethereum block 26214792 (2026-10-17T20:53:59Z), the dominant DOLA-paired Curve LP and Yearn-LP markets used Chainlink-derived USDe pricing, a fixed-$1 DOLA input, Curve virtual price and a guardian-operated FeedSwitchV2, not automatic outage failover. These two markets accounted for 74.706516% of issuer-reported FiRM debt, with constituent debts confirmed at that block; the denominator is the issuer API observation at Unix milliseconds 1792270364354, not a complete pinned debt census. PPO returns min(current price, today's/yesterday's recorded low divided by collateral factor) for nonzero collateral factor; this bounds borrowing power by min(current price times collateral factor, recorded low), rather than applying the collateral factor after a simple trailing-low minimum. Zero collateral factor bypasses damping; missing daily observations do not form an exact rolling 48-hour minimum. Other market-specific feed configurations remain incompletely reviewed.

branchApplicability.rationale: G1-3/G1-4: FiRM's isolated borrower markets require collateral-pricing branches. Ethereum block 26214792 (2026-10-17T20:53:59Z) resolves the dominant sUSDe-DOLA Curve LP and Yearn-wrapped LP feed paths separately from the common PPO and liquidation architecture retained for other markets. The common architecture is not a complete per-market feed census, and the issuer API debt denominator is separately observed rather than inferred from those two pinned markets.

branches.summary: G1-4: the common Oracle source at Ethereum block 26214792 (2026-10-17T20:53:59Z) dampens borrowing power using today's and yesterday's recorded lows and collateral factor. This branch preserves the documented isolated-market mechanics outside the separately reviewed dominant LP pair; it does not certify every remaining market's feed or fallback.

feeds.path: Configured external collateral feed -> min(current price, recorded daily low * 10000 / collateralFactorBps) for nonzero collateral factor -> FiRM market; zero collateral factor bypasses damping

branches.fallbackBehavior: G1-4: today's and yesterday's recorded daily lows bound borrowing power, not an exact rolling 48-hour price history or an independent fallback provider. No automatic failover is established by the common PPO source; per-market configurations outside the separately reviewed LP pair remain subject to verification.

collateralParameters.note: Each isolated market has governance-set collateral factor, liquidation factor, liquidation incentive, supply ceiling, and daily borrow limits; values differ by collateral and are not collapsed into one estimate.

branches.liquidationMechanism: When a loan breaches its market collateral factor, third-party liquidators repay DOLA debt and receive collateral plus the market liquidation incentive; depleted DBR can first trigger repeated permissionless replenishment that adds DOLA debt until liquidation eligibility is reached.
branches.backstop: For governance-approved FiRM markets, jrDOLA is a voluntary first-loss DOLA vault whose assets can be slashed to repay liquidation shortfalls; uncovered losses outside that coverage remain a claim on protocol reserves.
branches.shutdownOrBadDebtBehavior: FiRM isolates collateral markets so a market shortfall does not directly pool collateral risk across borrowers. Selected bad debt can slash jrDOLA before protocol reserves; reviewed documentation does not describe a global DOLA shutdown or holder settlement path.

branches.fallbackBehavior: G1-3: FeedSwitchV2 toggleFeedSwitch() is guardian-only; timelockPeriod() = 0, but latestRoundData() follows the selected feed, not automatic outage detection. The primary wrapper has hasFallback() = false and assetToUsdFallback() = zero; the alternative sUSDe computation also uses Chainlink infrastructure. CurveLPPessimisticFeed requires both coin inputs and propagates their older timestamp: a reverting/stale input does not automatically select an independent alternative. Hence standard-external ('a standard external feed'), not redundant-with-failover ('redundant feeds with automatic failover').

branches.liquidationMechanism: The reviewed FiRM market source and common documented liquidation architecture apply to these isolated LP markets: third-party liquidators repay DOLA debt against eligible undercollateralized positions and receive collateral plus the market-specific incentive. Depleted DBR can first trigger permissionless replenishment that adds debt until liquidation eligibility. The source-reviewed borrower credit gate is collateral value times collateralFactorBps / 10000 (Ethereum block 26214783, 2026-10-17T20:51:59Z; MintOnchainA active-market review).
branches.backstop: The common FiRM documentation describes jrDOLA as a voluntary first-loss vault that may be slashed for governance-approved market shortfalls before protocol reserves. This branch does not independently establish currently funded jrDOLA capacity or exact coverage of either LP market; those amounts and coverage remain unverified, not zero or guaranteed.
branches.shutdownOrBadDebtBehavior: These remain isolated FiRM borrower markets under the common documented bad-debt architecture. Selected covered shortfalls may slash jrDOLA before protocol reserves, but the LP-feed review does not establish a global DOLA shutdown, an automatic holder settlement path, or guaranteed recovery of either market's bad debt. Zero liquidationDelaySec denotes no additional protocol waiting period in the retained common liquidation mechanism, not assured keeper execution or collateral liquidity.
